title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures No. 2) Bill 2018
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures No. 2) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would address tax advantages from cross-border differences in tax treatment, and change film production concessions, cricket-related tax exemptions and deductible gift recipient listings.
Hybrid mismatch rules would deny deductions or add assessable income where payments produced duplicated deductions or deductions without corresponding taxable income in another country.
Most mismatch rules would apply for income years starting from 1 January 2019, with some imported mismatch arrangements deferred until years starting from 1 January 2020.
changes: Certain foreign branch income exemptions and deductions for Australian branches of foreign banks would be restricted.
Foreign tax deductions could prevent Australian franking benefits and tax exemptions for certain equity distributions.
Specified offshore film services supplied through companies would need to be performed by Australian residents to qualify for the producer offset.
Conditional income and withholding tax exemptions would cover the International Cricket Council's subsidiary, ICC Business Corporation FZ-LLC, for five years to support the 2020 tournament.
Qualifying gifts to Melbourne Korean War Memorial Committee Incorporated during 2018 and 2019 would become tax deductible.
summary.affected: Entities using covered cross-border arrangements, film production companies, ICC Business Corporation FZ-LLC and donors to Melbourne Korean War Memorial Committee Incorporated would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Leigh
speeches.brief: Labor will support the bill but move an amendment to change the start date of schedule 3 from 1 July 2017 to 1 July 2018, citing lack of consultation and retrospectivity; the speaker also criticised the government for missing the original implementation date on hybrid mismatch rules and for voting against Labor’s earlier multinational tax measures, including the Chevron case that secured $300 million.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The Treasury Laws Amendment (Tax Integrity and Other Measures No. 2) Bill 2018 was argued to improve tax system sustainability and integrity, implementing OECD hybrid mismatch rules to prevent multinational tax avoidance, clarifying the producer offset for overseas filming, providing a five-year income tax exemption for an International Cricket Council subsidiary to host the 2020 ICC World Twenty20, and listing the Melbourne Korean War Memorial Committee as a deductible gift recipient until 31 December 2019.
